title: Free City of Krakow
capsule: The Free City of Cracow (Wolne Miasto Kraków) was a nominally sovereign city-state established by the Congress of Vienna on 3 May 1815 from a core of the former Duchy of Warsaw, constituting the only republican government in Polish history prior to the twentieth century. Governed by an elected Assembly of Representatives and an executive Senate, it functioned as a jointly supervised protectorate of Russia, Prussia, and Austria, who intervened repeatedly to impose more restrictive constitutions (notably in 1833) and maintained occupation forces. Cracow served as a staging ground for Polish national activities, most consequentially during the Kraków Uprising of February 1846; Austria suppressed the revolt and annexed the city on 16 November 1846, incorporating it as the Grand Duchy of Kraków — an annexation condemned by Britain and France but ratified by a secret 1835 Austro-Russian-Prussian agreement.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The city-state's territory is well-defined by the 1815 Congress of Vienna act and subsequent protocols; boundaries and political status are clearly documented in diplomatic records.
